document: City of Vancouver Street Tree Guidelines for the Public Realm, Year 2011 Revision
relation_to_edm_table_9_3: The 2011 list groups species as Large / Medium / Small / Columnar / Conifers with class-level size thresholds; EDM 2026 Table 9-3 (33 species, no dimensions, no Columnar column) is the rule the tool applies. Where both list a species the classes are compared in data/species/<id>.json (guidelines_2011.agrees_with_table_9_3).

species_list.heading: Preferred Street Tree Species List
species_list.caveat: This list is to be used only as a general guide. Other species/cultivars may do well on streets. Trees listed as unsuitable may be fine for park or garden settings. (p.12)

Large.definition: Trees over 50 ' in height and 25 ' in width. Suitable for boulevards with no overhead obstructions and > 10 ' of width.

Medium.definition: Trees maturing between twenty-five (25) and fifty (50) feet are generally suitable for situating on a blockside tree lawn three (3) feet or greater between curb and sidewalk.

Small.definition: Trees maturing twenty-five (25) feet. Suitable for locating at or below overhead electrical conductors

Columnar.definition: Trees exhibiting a distinct upright branch arrangement. Suitable for locating in confined situations or on tree lawns offset from overhead electrical conductors.

Conifers.definition: Cone bearing trees are not generally planted on boulevards due to their low branching habit when young. Nonetheless, they are a desirable type of tree top plant where space allows. Traffic medians are often suitable.

entries.botanical: Malus X Floribunda (Disease Resistant Cultivar Recommendations Available)

spacing.heading: Minimum Spacing (Tree size category / Average Spacing)
spacing.general: minimum of 7 metres (p.3); spacing is considered on a site average scale, preference is to match existing tree spacing (p.8)

clearances.heading: preferred minimum distances trees should be planted from
clearances.curb: The curb side edge of a tree surround must be at least 0.15 metres from the back of the curb. (p.9)

root_barriers.text: Root barriers must be installed at the time of planting whenever a tree is installed within 2 metres of a sidewalk or other hardscape feature – excluding roads; or where specified on approved drawings.

underground_note.text: drain tiles, underground sprinkling systems, street lighting conduit, and some other electrical ducts are not shown on utility drawings, but are usually located directly behind the curb, which is very close to, and sometimes within, the street tree planting area.

protection_barrier.heading: MINIMUM PROTECTION REQUIRED – parallel to curb (excerpted from Bylaw #9958)
protection_barrier.measured_at: distance of barrier from near edge of tree trunk, measured parallel to curb and 1.4 m above grade
protection_barrier.no_curb_or_sidewalk: the barrier will extend back to outer edge of the boulevard (p/l), or for the same distance as used parallel to curb, whichever is less (p.20)

engineered_soil.text: four piece cutout provides approximately 2 cubic meters of soil; Engineered Soil: 50–80 mm clear granite rock mixed 4:1 with Vancouver Street Tree Mix (loamy sand / sandy loam), excavate the subgrade to a depth of 400–600 mm; Standard Detail G9.2 shows 750 mm engineered soil under a sidewalk or bike path
